subject: Quality Radar: triage for prompt-suite regression + product asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quality radar — prompt-suite v3 A/B shows spike in billing hallucinations

Team,

Quick heads-up from the quality radar run last night: the prompt-suite v3 A/B (canary cohort) shows a measurable uptick in hallucinated billing instructions for enterprise customers. Signal: 0.9% -> 3.7% incorrect/unsafe billing suggestions in the sampled queries for billing-related prompts (see attached CSV for examples). The product ask: we need a cross-functional decision on whether to hold the wider rollout and, if we continue, what compensating controls we require in product and ops (e.g., post-generation guardrail, stricter acceptance criteria, or reduced exposure window).

Primary asks: 
- Product: define minimal acceptance criteria to clear a rollback/continue decision.
- Engineering: list short-term mitigations we can ship in 72 hours.
- Sales/CS: estimate customer impact and whether we should proactively notify affected customers (Sable Health is in the canary group).

Attachments: promptset_v3_examples.csv (sample failures)

I recommend a brief sync today to pick next steps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Quality
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quality radar — prompt-suite v3 A/B shows spike in billing hallucinations

Marissa — thanks for flagging and for the examples. I pulled the recent CS tickets from Sable Health and there are two new threads that look tied to these responses; they've reported "incorrect refund instructions" that require manual rework. From a customer-facing perspective this is material.

Immediate thoughts:
- I support pausing the wider rollout until we have a mitigant in place (either a guardrail filter or a conservative fallback to v2 for billing-related intents).
- If we pause, we should prepare a short external note to Sable Health with mitigation ETA and an offer for a manual review until auto-behavior is safe.

I can take point on customer comms and coordinate with CS. We should set an internal decision deadline: 48 hours.

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quality radar — prompt-suite v3 A/B shows spike in billing hallucinations

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for flagging and for the examples. I pulled the recent CS tickets from Sable Health...

Thanks for the context. Technical options (feasible in ~72h for quick mitigation):
- Short-term: Add a high-precision filter after generation that checks for payment/billing entity patterns and blocks or flags outputs that match risky templates. Low dev effort, medium false-positive risk.
- Medium-term: Weight-adjusted fallback that routes billing-related prompts to v2 (the more conservative model) for the next 7 days for the canary cohort. Requires minimal infra change (routing rule).
- Longer-term: Retrain / tune prompt anchors and augment training examples for the billing taxonomy; timeline 2–3 weeks.

Implementation constraints to note: routing fallback will increase token cost ~8% for affected requests; filter needs a small rule-set plus a telemetry hook to monitor false positives.

I can prototype the filter and a routing rule today and have a patch ready for review by EOD tomorrow.

-Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quality radar — prompt-suite v3 A/B shows spike in billing hallucinations

Thanks all — good options. For the product decision I want to keep the acceptance criteria concrete so the team can act quickly. Proposed minimal acceptance criteria to greenlight rollout for billing intents: 

1) End-to-end false-positive rate for billing instructions <= 1.0% in the canary sample (measured on a validated prompt set).
2) No high-severity customer-reported incidents tied to billing generation in rolling 24h window after deployment.
3) Guardrail filter reduces observed unsafe outputs by >= 60% on the sample set (or routing to v2 in scope).

If we cannot meet all three within 48 hours, we hold the rollout and notify affected customers with a mitigation timeline.

Action items and owners: 
- Markus: prototype filter + routing rule (ETA: EOD tomorrow) — will include telemetry hooks.
- Ben: draft external comms and coordinate with Sable Health; please include an offer for manual review.
- Marissa: run the validation harness against the patch and report metrics.

I've attached an SLO exception form to capture the decision in case leadership needs to sign off.

Attachments: slo-exception-form.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, M. Reyes <m.reyes@sablehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quality radar — prompt-suite v3 A/B shows spike in billing hallucinations

Looping in Sable Health so they have visibility to our plan. Short summary/disposition: 

- Decision: Hold wider rollout for billing intents until the acceptance criteria are met.
- Immediate mitigations: Markus will ship a high-precision post-generation filter + telemetry (prototype by EOD Tue, 2027-06-22). If filter cannot attain threshold, we will route billing intents to v2 for the canary cohort.
- Customer steps: our CS lead will offer manual review of flagged responses until the guardrail is validated.

Marissa will publish the validation results once Markus' patch is in a staging canary (expected 24–36h). We will reconvene at 48 hours to decide final unblock.

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
